subject: Post-demo: DPA clarifications — breach notice routing & subprocessor mapping
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@medsync.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@medsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications requested

Hi Elena / Tom — thanks again for the demo call earlier. Quick recap and the privacy/ops items you asked us to follow up on: 

1) Controller vs. processor: you asked us to confirm the responsibilities matrix for PII we process on behalf of MedSync (e.g., who is responsible for patient notifications vs. processing-level telemetry).
2) Breach notification timing: you asked whether Redwood can commit to a specific initial notification window and a full incident report SLA.
3) Subprocessors and residency: requested list of current subprocessors and whether any subprocessors for MedSync would be outside the EU/US regions.
4) Logging & retention: confirm typical retention windows for access logs, request logs, and model telemetry — and whether retention can be customized per contract.

Attaching our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) for your legal to review. Next steps we propose: 
- Tom: if you can flag the must-have vs. nice-to-have items in the DPA, we’ll prioritize.
- Elena: confirm whether MedSync expects Redwood to be a processor for all PII processing in the pilot, or if there are any controller-level responsibilities you need us to accept.
- We’ll loop in Legal (cc’d) and Solutions to map subprocessor impacts and provide a redline.

Proposed timeline: we can get a redline + subprocessor registry to you within 48 business hours after Tom’s notes. If helpful, we can arrange a short legal-to-legal call this week.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@medsync.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Harris <tharris@medsync.com>
Date: 2029-08-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications requested

Thanks Rishi — good recap. A few clarifying questions from our side (Tom and I discussed offline):

- Breach notification: MedSync needs initial acknowledgement to the controller security contact within 48 hours, and a full incident summary within 10 business days for high-impact incidents. Can Redwood confirm you can meet that cadence or suggest alternatives?
- Controller responsibilities: MedSync will remain the controller for patient data; Redwood will be a processor for inference-related handling. However, we need explicit language that confirms Redwood will support controller-initiated patient notifications (i.e., supply processed records, timelines).
- Subprocessors: please confirm whether any subprocessors handle data outside the US. For pilot scope, we need a list and an option to review/add any subprocessor that will process EU-resident data.
- Logging/retention: we typically require access logs retained for 24 months, request logs for 12 months, and audit trails be exportable on request. Can Redwood provide retention profiles and commercial options for extended retention?

Tom — I’ve attached a short summary from our procurement team (MedSync_DPA_summary.pdf). If Redwood can respond to the points above, we’ll schedule a legal-to-legal call.

Best,
Elena
VP Product, MedSync Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-16T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + DPA clarifications requested — MedSync asks

Rishi / Ben — thanks for the ping. Quick answers and proposed next steps below. I’m putting the legal recommendations in plain language you can share with MedSync this afternoon.

Short answers: 
- Breach notification: Redwood’s standard practice is initial incident acknowledgement within 48 hours and a full technical incident report within 7 business days for incidents classified as high severity. We can commit to the 48-hour ack. For the full report, we can agree to 10 business days contractually for enterprise customers if necessary; operationally we usually deliver within 7 business days.
- Controller support for notifications: Redwood will provide processed records, exportable artifacts, and a point-of-contact to support controller-initiated notifications. We will include a section in the DPA that documents the support steps (data extracts, timelines, and reasonable assistance).
- Subprocessor registry: attached is the current public subprocessor registry link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/legal/rdw-dpa-subprocessors. Current subprocessors processing infra/monitoring may be located in the US and EU. We will flag any subprocessor that would handle EU-resident data specifically and provide a restricted list for MedSync review.
- Retention profiles: we offer configurable retention tiers. Standard: access logs 12 months, request logs 6 months. Extended retention: access logs up to 24 months and request logs up to 12 months available as a contract add-on. Audit trail export is supported via secure link; we’ll add export SLAs in the DPA.

Next steps I will take this afternoon: 
1) Produce a redline of Redwood_DPA_v3 with explicit language for breach support and retention options (attaching Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.pdf).
2) Provide a marked subprocessor list indicating region and data types processed.
3) Offer dates for a legal-to-legal call (Thursday 08/17 or Friday 08/18) — please let me know what works.

Suggested message for Elena (you can send as reply): we can confirm 48-hour ack + contractual 10-business-day full report if that is a hard requirement; otherwise we will commit to operational 7-business-day delivery. We will provide the subprocessor list and redline within 48 business hours.

Action items for Rishi/Ben: share MedSync preferred timeframe for pilot kick-off and confirm whether the 10-business-day contractual window is a must-have. I’ll prepare the redline and subprocessor mapping for review and will be ready for a legal call if requested.

– Marissa
VP, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
